candidates.name: Massive-STEPS
candidates.what_it_holds: Global-scale POI check-in trajectories for 15 cities across 10 countries (Beijing, Shanghai, Istanbul, Jakarta, Bandung, Palembang, Tangerang, Kuwait City, Melbourne, Sydney, Moscow, New York, Petaling Jaya, Sao Paulo, Tokyo). ~2.63M check-ins total, 133k+ users, 620k+ POIs, drawn from the 2013 and 2018 Semantic Trails Dataset (Foursquare-sourced) plus Foursquare Open Source Places. Preprocessed city-level splits hosted on Hugging Face Datasets; repo has Python preprocessing scripts and benchmark code (next-POI-prediction models). Apache-2.0 license, active repo (README references 2024-2025 work).
candidates.why_useful: A genuinely global, multi-city geotagged check-in panel including tourism-heavy cities (Sydney, Istanbul, Sao Paulo, Tokyo, NYC) that could proxy cross-border travel share, visitor mix, or destination popularity shifts over 2013-2018 -- speaks to gap #20 (party size / group travel / cross-border share proxies via geotagged tourism datasets) and loosely to gap #5 (engagement/popularity proxies). Not point-in-time and dated (2013/2018), so only useful as a historical base-rate / methodology reference, not a live nowcast input.
candidates.geography: 15 cities, 10 countries (Asia, Europe, Middle East, Oceania, Americas)

candidates.name: Semantic Trails Dataset (semantic-trails)
candidates.what_it_holds: Source dataset behind Massive-STEPS: Foursquare-derived global-scale check-ins enriched with GeoNames/Wikidata geography and Schema.org venue-category mappings, in checkins.csv / venues.csv plus RDF/Turtle conversions; a public SPARQL endpoint (http://std.eurecom.fr/sparql) is also live. Actual CSV/TTL files are hosted on figshare, not committed to the repo. Apache-2.0 license; example records dated through Oct 2017.
candidates.why_useful: Larger, better-documented upstream source for the check-in data that Massive-STEPS subsets; worldwide coverage with population and category metadata could support a party-size / trip-type proxy or a cross-border destination-mix index (gap #20). Queryable via SPARQL without needing the full dump.
candidates.size_hint: not stated in README; feeds Massive-STEPS's 2.63M-checkin subset, so likely larger

candidates.name: scikit-mobility
candidates.what_it_holds: Python mobility-analysis toolkit (808 stars) with a bundled `data` module and `list_datasets()`/`load_dataset()` API; ships ready-to-load example datasets including `foursquare_nyc` (Foursquare check-ins of individuals moving in NYC) and `flow_foursquare_nyc` (derived flow/OD data), plus SF taxi and parking datasets and NYC spatial tessellation boundaries. Also supports loading arbitrary CDR/GPS/survey mobility data into standard TrajDataFrame/FlowDataFrame structures.
candidates.why_useful: Turns the NYC Foursquare check-in dataset (and any future check-in export) into an immediately usable flow/OD panel with a one-line loader -- useful as a acquisition method for building a tourism-flow or intra-city mobility proxy without hand-rolling parsing, and its FlowDataFrame generative models (gravity/radiation) could synthesize destination-choice baselines for comparison.
candidates.size_hint: n/a (tooling); foursquare_nyc dataset is the standard ~227k-checkin Yang et al. NYC subset
candidates.license: not confirmed (widely used academic-origin project, check repo LICENSE)

candidates.name: Sequential-Recommendation-Datasets
candidates.what_it_holds: Download-and-preprocess scripts (228 stars, Apache-2.0, archived read-only as of May 2023) for 35+ sequential-recommendation datasets, including Foursquare NYC and Tokyo check-ins and Gowalla, alongside Amazon/Yelp/MovieLens etc. Provides user- or time-based splitting and PyTorch DataLoader wrappers; does not host raw data itself, only pull/parse code.
candidates.why_useful: One-command pull-and-clean pipeline for the two classic location check-in datasets (Foursquare NYC/Tokyo, Gowalla) that other tourism-mobility repos (HGARN, scikit-mobility) reference informally -- useful as tooling to reconstruct those panels for a party-size or destination-choice cut.

candidates.name: HGARN (Hierarchical Graph Attention Recurrent Network for human mobility prediction)
candidates.what_it_holds: IEEE TITS 2024 paper code (25 stars, Python) for next-location prediction; trains/evaluates on the canonical Yang et al. 'NYC and Tokyo Check-in Dataset' (Foursquare-derived, TSMC2014), pointing readers to https://sites.google.com/site/yangdingqi/home/foursquare-dataset for the raw data rather than committing it.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms and links the standard, widely-used Foursquare NYC/Tokyo check-in dataset (with a working non-GitHub host) plus a modern (2024) modeling method that could be repurposed to score destination popularity/visit-sequence shifts as a mobility proxy.
candidates.size_hint: code only; dataset itself is the standard ~227k (NYC) / ~573k (Tokyo) checkin files

candidates.name: YFCC100M-Downloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tool (42 stars, last updated 2020-05-12) that downloads photos/videos and metadata from the YFCC100M (Yahoo Flickr Creative Commons 100 Million) dataset, filterable by metadata fields including geotags and timestamps.
candidates.why_useful: Working, non-scraper acquisition path for YFCC100M's geotagged Flickr photo/video metadata (100M items, worldwide, with capture timestamps) -- could be filtered to top tourism destinations for a photo-volume travel-flow proxy, one of the explicit theme targets (YFCC100M tourism subsets).
candidates.size_hint: n/a (downloader); parent dataset is 100M Flickr photos/videos with metadata

candidates.name: yfcc100m-downloader (stefanbirkner)
candidates.what_it_holds: Second, independent Python downloader (24 stars, last updated 2018-05-14) for YFCC100M metadata/media, simpler feature set than chi0tzp's tool.
candidates.why_useful: Redundant fallback acquisition method for YFCC100M if the primary downloader breaks or lacks a needed filter option.

candidates.name: flickr_scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python Flickr image scraper (298 stars) for building keyword-based image sets via the Flickr API, with pagination and deduplication; not geotag-specific but Flickr API responses include geo fields when present.
candidates.why_useful: Could be adapted to pull geotagged Flickr photos for specific tourism-city keywords/date ranges as a rough photo-volume travel proxy, though it is a general scraper rather than a tourism-purpose-built tool and would need location filtering added.

candidates.name: swarm-to-sqlite
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool (67 stars) that exports a user's own Foursquare Swarm check-in history into a local SQLite database via the Foursquare API.
candidates.why_useful: Only works for a single authenticated user's own history, not a bulk tourism dataset -- flagged for completeness as a Foursquare-adjacent acquisition method but not directly useful at panel scale.

notes: This session's shared WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this scout's queries could run, so this pass used WebFetch against github.com/topics/<tag> pages and direct repo READMEs instead of WebSearch -- coverage is narrower than a normal run (github.com/search full-text search returned HTTP 429 rate-limited for an hour on the first attempt, so repository search had to go through topic-tag pages, which only surface repos that authors explicitly tagged). Dead ends: github.com/topics/location-based-social-network, /checkin-data, and /geotagged-tweets are essentially empty or off-topic; DuckDuckGo HTML search returned a CAPTCHA wall; Bing search via WebFetch returned only generic GitHub marketing pages, not indexed results. Two guessed repo URLs (gombru/InstaCities1M for the Instagram city-classification dataset, multimedia-commons/multimedia-commons for official YFCC100M tooling, and perezluque/pySpainMobility) all 404'd -- worth a targeted retry by an agent with `gh search` or a working WebSearch budget, since InstaCities1M (Instagram-sourced, city-labeled images) and the official Yahoo/ICSI YFCC100M tooling repo are real and would likely be higher-value finds than what surfaced here. Also worth a follow-up: Twitter/X geotagged-tourism datasets turned up nothing substantive in this pass (Twitter's 2023 API paywall has killed most public geotagged-tweet dataset repos); TikTok tourism data had zero hits under any query attempted -- likely a dead vein on GitHub specifically. Massive-STEPS and its upstream Semantic Trails Dataset are the strongest finds and are worth a teammate's follow-up pull to check if the 15-city panel (esp. Sydney, Sao Paulo, Istanbul, Tokyo -- all ABNB-relevant tourism markets) can be extended past 2018 or cross-walked to modern quarters.
